title: Feature Explorer: rank real measurements and keep the comparison explicit
description: Open the Classify submodule, compare real plate-row measurements, inspect distributions, filter live, add a computed column and export the intended ranking without training a classifier.
objectives: Find Feature Explorer inside Classify and load existing cell measurements.
Distinguish AUC from separation, and inspect class counts and distribution differences.
Filter live without overlooking an automatic change of comparison column.
Use Top deliberately, verify a scaled computed column and export the actual ranking.
prerequisite: Use the downloaded Annotate example, not invented measurements. The recording opens a byte-identical private copy of its 2,341-cell, 276-column measurement database. The two rowID groups are spatial plate rows r12 and r5, not asserted treatments; cells share fields and wells and are not independent experiments. Original data remain unchanged. AUC, KS, ranking order and finite class counts are independently checked for the intended two-class comparisons. The automatically selected eight-class comparison is a warning example, not independently validated inference. Shuffle test stays off. No classifier training, new image analysis, dedicated download, GPU operation or AI request occurs here; the displayed histograms are the module's own plots.

scenes.narration: Open Classify, then its Feature Explorer button. This nested tool ranks existing measurements; opening it does not train a classifier. We use the real downloadable Annotate example on a private database copy. Follow the Annotate lesson to obtain the example, and keep your experimental source unchanged.

Choose Load table, select the measurement database and its cell table, then set Split by to rowID. There are two thousand three hundred forty-one cells and two hundred seventy-six columns. Our two groups are recorded plate rows, not established treatments; these cells are not independent experiments.

Rank by AUC and read both numeric columns. Separation is the absolute value of twice AUC minus one, so about zero point three four separation is not a zero point three four AUC. Higher in names the direction; min n counts finite measurements in the smaller class, not replicate experiments.

Set Top to four to inspect four overlaid histograms. Classes share the same bin edges within each feature, and bar heights are counts. The largest ranking is not automatically a useful biomarker. Read the warning: AUC can miss differences in spread even when the distributions differ.

Export ranking with Top four writes four feature rows. In this build the export follows Top, despite wording that suggests the whole ranking. It does not export the underlying cells or save a trained model. We compared every exported value with the actual current ranking.

Set Top to five hundred before exporting all scored features in this example. Two hundred sixty-one features can be scored; two numeric candidates cannot. The export contains all two hundred sixty-one rows, while the display draws at most eight distributions. Feature counts, table rows and plotted panels are different quantities.

Switch Rank by to KS to compare the largest gap between cumulative distributions, then return to AUC. KS can reveal distribution differences that AUC misses but does not provide direction itself. Other offered statistics have their own limitations; read the visible warning rather than treating a rank as a significance test.

In Filter, add cell_area and set the minimum to twenty-one thousand nine hundred twenty-five. The visible population changes to one thousand one hundred seventy-one cells, and two hundred fifty-five features remain scorable. This median-based demonstration threshold is not a biological quality cutoff. Rankings and distributions update without remeasuring images.

Clear all removes the display filters, not the data. All two thousand three hundred forty-one cells and the original ranking return. Recheck the population and Split by whenever you change filters. A difference that changes after filtering describes a different selected population, not a new experiment.

There is an important trap in this build. Filtering rowID to r12 removes the other row, but the screen silently switches Split by to cell_channel_0_maxima_count. It now compares eight groups, with only one object in the smallest. Those impressive scores are not the original row comparison or evidence of a biological discovery.

Clear the filter and explicitly choose rowID again. Clearing alone does not necessarily restore the original comparison. Verify both the class column and the population before exporting. Shuffle test offers fifty label shuffles, but we leave it off: freely shuffling these correlated cells would not establish well-level or treatment-level evidence.

Open Columns and name a new column area_k. Enter cell_area divided by one e three, meaning one thousand, and choose Add column with replacement off. This rescales area; it does not calibrate physical units or add a new measurement. Preview checks the first two thousand rows; adding applies the formula to the full table.

The scaled column joins the ranking and export, giving two hundred sixty-two scored features. Its AUC and KS equal those of cell_area because positive rescaling preserves order. We checked every computed value. Remove the formula to return to the original two hundred sixty-one features; the measurement database remains unchanged.

Use these rankings for descriptive exploration, not independent validation of a selected feature or a trained classifier. In Python, spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank provides rank_features and ExplorerSpec. For inspecting raw tables or drawing other comparisons, continue with Database Browser and Graph Builder. No new image-analysis pipeline or AI request was run.
